### Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP)

Offered through [Aetna Student Health](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$), PSIP meets Penn’s insurance requirement. For students in most graduate and professional programs, the cost of the health insurance plan is already incorporated into the cost-of-attendance budget used for purposes of financial aid and student loan eligibility. All students who enroll in PSIP will also be charged the clinical fee in order to access Student Health and Counseling as your primary care provider. Please check with your program’s financial aid office for details.

PhD students may be eligible for grants to assist with purchasing selected plans. Please review the [Insurance Grants Webpage](https://gsc.upenn.edu/resources/graduate-funding-and-finances/insurance-grants) to be sure you understand which plans are eligible and the full grant details.

For undergraduates, the Federal Direct Loan Program and Parent Loan Program (PLUS) may be available to help meet this expense, as long as the student has completed a FAFSA and connects with [Student Registration and Financial Services](https://srfs.upenn.edu/) to request a Cost of Attendance (COA) adjustment. In some cases, depending on the individual student’s level of financial need, grant assistance may be available to aided students. If you have any questions, contact [Student Registration and Financial Services](https://srfs.upenn.edu/DocumentSubmit).

[Visit the Aetna Student Health Site](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$)

[Enroll or waive in PSIP](https://studenthealth.bgenroll.com/home)

#### PSIP Details for 2026-2027

Specific claims questions regarding PSIP can be directed to the Aetna Student Health Customer Service team at [800-841-5374](tel:800-841-5374). Those enrolled can print their insurance card by going to the [Aetna Student Health website](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$).

### PSIP Plan Enroll/Waive Period

The Insurance Portal opens and closes at various points throughout the year:

- July 1 - August 31 for Fall semester enrollees

- December 16 - January 31 for Spring semester enrollees

- April 15 - May 31 for Summer semester enrollees

The [Clinical Fee](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-requirements/new-and-incoming-students#:~:text=The%20clinical%20fee%20for%20the%202026%2D2027%20academic%20year%20will%20be%20%24385%20per%20semester) and the Student Health and Counseling eligibility periods match these schedules, as well.

### PSIP Rates

Single student coverage:

- Annual: effective August 1, 2026 - July 31, 2027: premium rate $5,018

- Spring semester: effective January 1, 2027 - July 31, 2027: premium rate $2,915

- Summer semester: effective May 1, 2027 - July 31, 2027: premium rate $1,265

Enrollment deadlines:

- Fall semester deadline: August 31

- Spring semester deadline: January 31

- Summer semester deadline: May 31

Supplemental Coverage for July

Graduate students starting University programs in July may enroll in the summer plan at a prorated premium for the month of July. Please contact the Immunization and Insurance Navigators at [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355), or email us at [wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu) for more information and to obtain an application.

Note: If you are in a program that is paying for your insurance, please check with your school to make certain they will cover this supplemental coverage.

### Students on Leave of Absence (LOA)

Students on approved LOA who would like to purchase the health insurance plan offered through the University must reach out directly to our Insurance Navigators for a LOA Insurance application by calling [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) or emailing [wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu](https://wellness.upenn.edu/public-health-and-wellbeing/wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu).

### Dependent Rates

Dependent coverage:

- Annual: effective August 1, 2026 - July 31, 2027

  - Premium rate for spouse/domestic partner: $5,018

  - Premium rate for one child: $5,018

  - Premium rate for two or more children: $10,036

- Spring semester: effective January 1, 2027 - July 31, 2027

  - Premium rate for spouse/domestic partner: $2,915

  - Premium rate for one child: $2,915

  - Premium rate for two or more children: $5,830

- Summer semester: effective May 1, 2027 - July 31, 2027

  - Premium rate for spouse/domestic partner: $1,265

  - Premium rate for one child: $1,265

  - Premium rate for two or more children: $2,530

Dependent premiums are paid directly to Aetna Student Health. They are not posted to student bursar accounts. Rates do not include single student base premium.

### Enrollment of Dependents

Penn students utilizing the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP) may enroll their lawful spouse/domestic partner and unmarried dependent children under age 26 who reside with, and are fully supported by, the covered student for the same coverage. Student must be enrolled in PSIP before they can enroll spouses or dependents.

Dependent enrollment is processed online at [www.aetnastudenthealth.com/upenn](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$). All spouses and domestic partners must have a Penn Guest Card to determine dependent status. Students will need to submit a Dependent Enrollment Application with payment directly to Aetna. Contact Aetna at [(800) 841-5374](tel:(800) 841-5374) with any questions regarding dependent enrollment. Dependent premiums may be paid in full or in monthly installments.

- Fall semester deadline: August 31

- Spring semester deadline: January 31

- Summer semester deadline: May 31

The Dependent Enrollment Application and premium will not be accepted after the deadline unless there is a qualifying life event, including the following:

- involuntary loss of health insurance

- marriage

- entry into the US

A certificate of credible coverage stating the date of the involuntary loss of health coverage, marriage certificate or stamped passport along with a signed application must be submitted to Aetna Student Health within 31 days of the qualifying life event. After the 31 days, the dependent would no longer eligible for enrollment in the current policy year.

### Newborn Infant and Adopted Child Coverage

A child born to a Covered Person shall be covered for Preventative Care, Accident, Sickness, and congenital defects, for 31 days from the date of birth. At the end of this 31 day period, coverage will cease under the University of Pennsylvania Student Health Insurance Plan. To extend coverage for a newborn past the 31 days, the covered student must:

1. Enroll the child within 31 days of birth, AND

2. Pay the additional premium, starting from the date of birth

Coverage is provided for a child legally placed for adoption with a covered student for 31 days from the moment of placement provided the child lives in the household of the covered student, and is dependent upon the covered student for support. To extend coverage for an adopted child past the 31 days, the covered student must:

1. Enroll the child within 31 days of placement of such child, AND

2. Pay any additional premium, if necessary, starting from the date of placement.

For information or general questions on dependent enrollment, contact Aetna Student Health at [(800) 841-5374](tel:(800) 841-5374).

### Dental Coverage for Students

For academic year 2026-2027, students may voluntary enroll themselves and their dependents in the Penn Student Dental Plan or the Aetna Student Dental Plan.

Penn Student Dental Plan

- Please go to [www.mypenndentist.org](http://www.mypenndentist.org/) for details. Note: All services for this plan are rendered by Penn Dental Family Practice and this plan cannot be used elsewhere. This is plan is not affiliated with Aetna or PSIP.

Aetna Student Health Dental Plan

- You don’t have to be enrolled in PSIP to enroll in the Aetna Student Dental Plan. You can use this plan nationwide. Please go to the [Aetna Student Health website](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$) for details.

Vital Savings Discount Program

- Aetna offers the Vital Savings Discount Program as an option for students to purchase on a voluntary basis. This is a discount program, not insurance. Please note: Penn Dental Family Practice does not accept this discount program. Please go to [Aetna Student Health](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$) for more information.

### Aetna Vision Preferred

For academic year 2026-2027, students may voluntary enroll themselves and their dependents in the Aetna Vision Preferred Plan. This plan is open to all students, you don’t have to be enrolled in the PSIP insurance plan to enroll in the vision plan. View the [A](https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/school/724535/members/enroll-waive-coverage.html)[etna Student Health](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/upenn/index.html__;!!IBzWLUs!VNBy5dFfO-Q0s_tWNLrDbdYXAB78gfxTmvzBeo76GzE9jBXCVRHtIXSbJUKjnZW9g6UvhbPB94piVipZrN-0euE$) page.

### Student Health Insurance Advisory Committee (SHIAC)

Sponsored by the Provost, SHIAC brings together students, faculty, and staff to review and guide the [Penn Student Health Insurance Plan (PSIP)](https://wellness.upenn.edu/insurance-requirements/penn-student-insurance-plan-psip). Chaired by the Vice Provosts for Education, the committee evaluates and negotiates the plan annually, ensuring it remains affordable, comprehensive, and responsive to student needs. SHIAC also serves as a forum for addressing emerging health insurance issues and exploring improvements in a rapidly changing landscape. Suggestions and questions can be emailed to [shiac@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:shiac@pobox.upenn.edu).

### Personal Navigator Program for Students

The Personal Navigator program connects students directly to one single point of contact to assist in non-clinical, clinical, and behavioral health resources. This program helps to reduce barriers many students may face in accessing the care, services, and procedures needed.

The Personal Navigators are accessible through the regular Customer Service number ([800-841-5374](tel:800-841-5374)).

### Other Resources

[Affordable Care Act FAQ](https://www.healthcare.gov/young-adults/college-students/)

[Student Health and Counseling Forms](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-compliance/medical-forms)

[Doc Find](https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/school/724535/members/find-doctor.html)

#### Dental and Vision Insurance Coverage for Fully Funded PhD Students

Learn more about insurance coverage options for fully funded PhD students by visiting the [Graduate Student Center's insurance information page](https://gsc.upenn.edu/graduate-funding-and-finances#phd).

## 2026-2027 Academic Year

All full-time and dissertation-status students, and exchange students here for a semester or more, must carry comprehensive health insurance as a condition of student enrollment at the University of Pennsylvania. If you have your own insurance coverage, you may waive enrollment in the Penn Student Insurance Plan. Please review the information below.

Please note: the PSIP portal will be open from July 1 through August 31 for students enrolled in the fall 2026 semester.

[Enroll or Waive Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP)](https://studenthealth.bgenroll.com/home)

[About PSIP, Vision, and Dental Plan](https://wellness.upenn.edu/insurance-requirements/penn-student-insurance-plan-psip)

[Student Health and Counseling Forms](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-compliance/medical-forms)

[Access Your PSIP Insurance Card](https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/school/724535/members/get-id-card.html)

##### Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the University’s insurance criteria?

Students in the Philadelphia area must have insurance that meets the following standards. If you are covered under your own health insurance or that of your parents, you may maintain your coverage if it meets the following criteria:

- Your insurance plan must be provided by a company licensed to do business in the United States, with a U.S. claims payment office and a U.S. telephone number. The company must have a process to remit payments to providers within the U.S.

- Your insurance plan must provide coverage for pre-existing conditions, or have been in effect long enough that any waiting period has passed.

- Your insurance plan must offer an annual maximum benefit of at least $2,000,000.

- Your insurance plan must provide for both in-patient and out-patient mental health care in the Philadelphia area. A policy that provides only emergency or urgent mental health care services in this area does not meet this requirement. *

- Your insurance plan must provide coverage for both in-patient and out-patient medical care in the Philadelphia area, including routine office visits, specialist office visits, diagnostic testing, imaging and physical therapy. A policy that provides only emergency or urgent medical care in this area does not meet this requirement.*

*If you are insured with an out-of-area managed care plan (i.e. HMO or similar plan), you should be aware that most managed care plans do not cover any care outside of the plan network other than urgent and emergency services. Unless your insurance carrier provides you with a rider for out-of-area coverage in the Philadelphia area, your waiver will not be approved.

### What is the Clinical Fee?

Wellness' [Student Health and Counseling](https://wellness.upenn.edu/student-health-and-counseling) division is committed to partnering with you to treat illnesses and injuries, promote wellness, and provide you with health education and information. Access is provided through Penn's Clinical Fee. The clinical fee for the 2026-2027 academic year will be $385 per semester. All full-time students, including those who are enrolled in the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP), will be charged the Clinical Fee.

### What do I need to know before I enroll into or waive out of the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP)?

Students must enroll into or waive out of the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP) every year. If you waive out of PSIP, you will be asked to submit your health insurance for verification that it meets the University requirements.

You will need to have a PennKey and password to access the Penn Student Insurance Portal. The PennKey is your link to most of the electronic resources that you will need while here on campus. If you are a first year student, contact your school to find out how to obtain a PennKey (or visit the [PennKey website](https://pennkeysupport.upenn.edu/help-for-students).)

IMPORTANT: If you receive a message stating that you don’t have access to this site, this may be because we have not yet received your registration information from the University. Please try back in few days. If the problem persists longer than a week, please contact the Insurance Navigators at [215-746-4200](tel:215-746-4200) or email us at [wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu).

If your health insurance changes at any point during the academic year, your coverage must be updated in person in the Immunization and Insurance Compliance Office. You cannot change the date of enrollment. Once you have completed your selection, you will receive a confirmation email. You can also visit the Insurance Portal again to view your selection information and the status of your waiver request.

If you are a student enrolling in the Penn Student Insurance Plan, please be aware that you will also be charged the Clinical Fee in order to access Student Health and Counseling as your primary care provider.

The Insurance Portal opens and closes at various points throughout the year:

- July 1 - August 31 for Fall semester and annual plan enrollees

- December 15 - January 31 for Spring semester enrollees

- April 15 - May 31 for Summer semester enrollees

### How do I enroll in or waive the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP)?

You can enroll in or waive the Penn Student Insurance Plan by clicking the links at the top of this page.

Please note: the Insurance Portal opens and closes at various points throughout the year:

- July 1 - August 31 for Fall semester and annual plan enrollees

- December 15 - January 31 for Spring semester enrollees

- April 15 - May 31 for Summer semester enrollees

If you would like to waive, please obtain a copy of your plan’s benefits and review them to ensure your plan meets the necessary criteria. Please note that all waiver requests must be approved by the University. The University audits waiver requests and may contact your insurance company to verify that your plan meets the University’s insurance criteria. Alternate insurance plans found to not meet these criteria will not be approved.

It is your responsibility to inform us of any change in your insurance during the academic year.

Watch this instructional video to find out how to complete your Insurance enrollment or waiver!

### What are the referral requirements?

Students covered under the Penn Student Insurance Plan should first seek medical treatment at Student Health and Counseling for each medical condition if within 25 miles of Student Health and Counseling. The Student Health and Counseling provider will refer you, if appropriate, to an outside provider in advance of your appointment. A new referral for each condition is required at the beginning of each policy year.

Any care received within 25 miles of Student Health and Counseling without a prior Student Health and Counseling referral will be payable subject to the Non-Preferred Benefit, including the $1,500 Deductible.

A referral is not required in the following circumstances:

- Treatment for an emergency medical condition

- The student is more than 25 miles away from Student Health and Counseling

- Annual eye exams, services, and supplies

- Injury to sound natural teeth or removal of impacted wisdom teeth

- Preventive or routine services

- Reproductive health and voluntary termination of pregnancy

- Inpatient and outpatient mental health and substance use services

- Pediatric care

- Students on leave of absence

- Outpatient lab services

- Care for dependents

The referral requirement does not apply to covered dependents or when Student Health and Counseling is closed. Referrals expire July 31. Please contact Student Health and Counseling for all questions about referrals.

### How do I print my PSIP insurance card?

Those enrolled can print their insurance card by going to the [Aetna Student Health website](https://www.aetnastudenthealth.com/en/school/724535/members/get-id-card.html)

### A Qualifying Life Event (Loss of Coverage)

A Qualifying Life Event is an involuntary loss of health insurance coverage such as:

- Removal from parents health insurance coverage after achieving a landmark birthday

- Losing health insurance through loss of employment or divorce

- A change in private insurance from a PPO to an HMO, which is not covered in the Philadelphia area.

To request an application please email or call our Insurance Navigators:

[215-746-4200](tel:215-746-4200)

Insurance: [wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu](https://wellness.upenn.edu/public-health-and-wellbeing/wel-shsinsur@pobox.upenn.edu)

*All applications must be received within 31 days of the Qualifying Life Event.

##### Tips for International Students

International Students residing in the US may be eligible for plans offered by PSI and ISO. While these plans are accepted by the University and meet the waiver requirements, they are not sponsored by the University of Pennsylvania, they are merely a suggestion of international private insurance plans that will meet the requirements of the University (whichever plan you choose it must cover your stay as a Student at UPenn):

- [PSI Emerald, Platinum, and Presidential](https://www.psiservice.com/portal.do?schoolId=School00490)

- [ISO Plans For UPenn](https://www.isoa.org/university_of_pennsylvania)

##### Health Insurance Terms and Definitions

[View our list](https://upenn.box.com/v/health-insurance-terms) of common terms used in relation to health insurance with brief and general definitions. A more comprehensive glossary of health care terms can be found on the [HealthCare.gov website](https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/).

##### Tips for English Language Program (ELP) Students

If you receive your health insurance through the English Language Program (ELP), you will receive your card in your mail folder in the Student Center. You will also receive a second card in a few weeks that you can use to help pay for prescription medications at the pharmacy.

Registering your ELP Insurance Policy

[Register your ELP insurance policy](https://www.geobluetravelinsurance.com/memberservices_preview.cfm) when you receive your card. This is very important because you must do this in order to use your insurance card. You can also find information on this website about what services are covered by your insurance and how to request reimbursement (the company may pay you back for some services)

##### Seeking care at Student Health and Counseling versus an Emergency Room

A Penn Student Health and Counseling provider is on-call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week to aid students in deciding if and where they should go to have their medical needs addressed. If it is a true medical emergency, students should call Penn Comm at [215-573-3333](tel:215-573-3333) if on campus, call 9-1-1 if outside the Penn patrol zone, or head to the nearest emergency room, preferably one in the Penn Medicine network (Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania at 34th and Spruce, or Presbyterian at 38th and Market).

###### Contact the Immunization and Insurance Navigators

Philadelphia PA 19104

You can learn more about our support services here:

- Monday: 9 am – 7:30 pm

- Tuesday: 9 am – 7:30 pm

Call [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) to schedule an appointment or to speak to a counseling provider at any time of the day or night, 24/7. If you’ve already been seen at our medical care office, you can now schedule future appointments online through your [PennChart account](https://secure.mypennmedicine.org/MyPennMedicine/Authentication/Login?).

Location: [3535 Market Street, Suite 100, Philadelphia, PA 19104](https://www.google.com/maps?q=3535+Market+Street,%C2%A0Suite+100,%C2%A0Philadelphia,+PA+19104&sxsrf=ALiCzsZWTsbhOWPjuleZztz6JS5pedU_5g:1667841654940&uact=5&gs_lcp=Cgxnd3Mtd2l6LXNlcnAQAzIFCAAQgAQ6BAgAEEc6CggAEEcQ1gQQsAM6DQgAEEcQ1gQQyQMQsANKBAhBGABKBAhGGABQ1yVY1yVglCxoAnACeACAAVOIAVOSAQExmAEAoAECoAEByAEIwAEB&um=1&ie=UTF-8&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjl0a-uypz7AhUcElkFHbQ1DGMQ_AUoAXoECAEQAw)

### What medical services does Wellness provide?

Wellness provides a wide range of clinical services to support our students. If you have questions, please reach out to our offices by calling 215-746-WELL (9355). Below is a list of services that students can receive through our medical care office. [View more information about our services here](https://wellness.upenn.edu/medical-care/all-medical-services). Please note: you will be prompted to log in with your Penn Key.

- Allergy Injections

- Gynecologic Care

- Immunizations

- LGBTQ+ Care

- Primary Care

- Nutrition

- Primary Care

- Sexual Health

- Sports Medicine

- Travel Medicine

### After Hours Care

If you need medical care when our office is closed:

### Call with urgent questions that cannot wait.

We always have a person on call to address urgent medical questions. For example, if you are not sure whether your symptoms should warrant an immediate visit to a hospital Emergency Room, the on-call provider can help you figure out what to do. Simply call our main phone number [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) to be connected to our provider on call.

### Visit a local Urgent Care.

There are several options in Philadelphia (you can search online for them), and their hours vary. Remember that you and your health insurance plan are responsible for any costs related to this care. Following are some examples, but listing them here does not imply endorsement of the services provided there:

- [Vybe Urgent Care Center City](https://www.vybe.care/locations/center-city/)

- [Jefferson Urgent Care at Rittenhouse](https://www.jeffersonhealth.org/locations/rittenhouse-urgent-care)

- [Jefferson Urgent Care at Washington Square](https://www.jeffersonhealth.org/locations/washington-square-urgent-care)

### Go to the nearest Emergency Room or call 9-1-1 if it's a true medical emergency.

Patients can be evaluated and possibly admitted into the hospital for more intensive treatment. Remember that you and your health insurance plan are responsible for any costs related to this care. Emergency Rooms should not be used for mild conditions that can wait until our office re-opens for business. We recommend one of the following Emergency Departments:

- [Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania (HUP)](https://www.pennmedicine.org/practices/emergency-medicine-hup-pavilion?utm_source=location-management&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=penn-medicine&utm_term=emergency-medicine-hup-pavilion&y_source=1_NDE5Nzk1Mi03MTUtbG9jYXRpb24ud2Vic2l0ZQ%3D%3D) – 1 Convention Avenue, Philadelphia

- [Penn Presbyterian Medical Center (PPMC)](https://www.pennmedicine.org/practices/emergency-medicine-penn-presbyterian?fadf=pennmedicine)– Myrin Building, 51 N. 39th Street, Philadelphia

- [Pennsylvania Hospital (PAH)](https://www.pennmedicine.org/practices/emergency-medicine-pennsylvania-hospital?fadf=pennmedicine) – 800 Spruce Street, Philadelphia

If you are experiencing a medical emergency, call PennComm (24/7) at [215-573-3333](tel:215-573-3333). Dial 911 if outside of the Penn patrol zone. If you are experiencing a suicidal crisis or are in emotional distress, contact the national Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (24/7) dial 988 or [chat with a national Suicide and Crisis Lifeline support person(link is external)](https://suicidepreventionlifeline.org/chat/). You can also text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counselor (24/7).

### Medical Care Appointments

##### 24/7 Support

Call [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) or schedule your medical care appointment online through your [PennChart account](https://secure.mypennmedicine.org/MyPennMedicine/Authentication/Login?).

### Instructions for NEW PATIENTS to schedule your online appointment:

1. Download the MyChart app in the App Store or Google Play or visit the [PennChart website](https://secure.mypennmedicine.org/MyPennMedicine/Authentication/Login?).

2. Log into (or create) your myPennMedicine account.

3. Once logged in, click on “Schedule an Appointment” and then select “All Options.”

# Welcome to Penn!

We are thrilled that you are embarking on your next adventure as a Quaker. Wellness at Penn is dedicated to caring for students during their academic journey while creating a campus-wide community of care. Our team is committed to offering a wide range of opportunities to access support, clinical resources, education, and practical tools to meaningfully engage with one's health and wellbeing.

Before your arrival to campus, all full- and part-time students should do the following (you can find all information to complete these tasks below):

- [Activate your PennChart account](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-requirements/new-and-incoming-students#:~:text=Activate%20PennChart%20Account)

- [Complete immunization requirements](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-requirements/new-and-incoming-students#:~:text=after%2024%20hours.-,Immunization%20Requirements,-The%20forms%20below)

- [Enroll in or waive the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP) annually](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-requirements/new-and-incoming-students#:~:text=Annual%20Insurance%20Requirements)

To ensure the health and safety of all students, the University requires all full- and part-time students to have adequate health insurance and remain up-to-date on their immunizations. Review instructions for uploading your immunization records and completing your health information requirements below.

## Activate PennChart Account

Through your PennChart account, you can access your Student Health and Counseling records and upload and manage your immunization records.

[Activate Your PennChart](https://upenn-support.freshdesk.com/support/tickets/new?ticket_form=pennchart_account_activation_request_form)

After you fill out this form, you will receive an email from our team with next steps within 2 business days. If you have questions, you can reach out to our Immunization Navigators by calling [215-746-4200](tel:215-746-4200) or emailing [wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu). You can also visit them in person at 3535 Market Street, Mezzanine, Suite 60.

## Immunization Requirements

The forms below contain information about the university required and recommended vaccinations. Penn requires all full- and part-time undergraduate and graduate students to be vaccinated with certain immunizations before arriving to campus. The forms linked below must be printed, completed, and reviewed and signed by a medical provider. You can also visit our [Immunization Requirements FAQ page](https://wellness.upenn.edu/faqs-immunization-requirements) for more information.

Please note: clinical students enrolling in the nursing program, the Dental School, PSOM, the School of Nursing, or the Vet School have different requirements. If entering vaccinations that are not listed as required/recommended on the form, please enter the dates of vaccination and submit appropriate documentation.

##### Universal (Non-Clinical/Non-Healthcare Student) Immunization Form

- [Universal Immunization Requirements: 2026-2027](https://upenn.box.com/s/vuf3dn6c0sn0vinekn4qp8tjequhwr8l)

##### Clinical/Healthcare Student Immunization Forms

Each School's form will be posted prior to the 2026-2027 academic year.

- [Dental School Immunization Requirements: 2026-2027](https://upenn.box.com/s/8hpmb9gv6f3bg7rcl4u4dhcqe83d7uzy)

- [PSOM Immunization Requirements: 2026-2027](https://upenn.box.com/s/dyrovecyno8machf38qfzeoa9ma4iqb9) Please note: these requirements are specific to the BioMed, GENC, Med, and MPHY programs. All other PSOM programs should follow the Universal Requirements form above.

- [School of Nursing Immunization Requirements: 2026-2027](https://upenn.box.com/s/z0xdt1unr0u34qi5qu5jxkb3nw3u8fmf)

- [Veterinary School Immunization Requirements: 2026-2027](https://upenn.box.com/s/bb92cy7x9pizf2q3n62793ok4zecrkzr)

##### Submission Instructions

### Step 1: Contact your medical provider.

- Print the necessary immunization requirement form from the list above, complete the information, and have your medical provider review and sign it.

- Ask your medical provider for a copy of your full immunization records. Your provider should use the immunization form to provide a clearer picture of your immunization records prior to completing step 3.

- Scan or take a high-resolution photo of your complete and signed immunization form and other immunization records (please make certain the copy is legible and right side up).

### Step 2: Submit your immunization documents before your arrival to campus.

- Go to your [PennChart](https://secure.mypennmedicine.org/MyPennMedicine/Authentication/Login?) and log in. Please note: you will be directed to your PennChart through myPennMedicine. If you do not have an account, you will need to click on "Activate an Account."

- Once logged in, follow these [Immunization Requirements Submission Instructions](https://upenn.box.com/s/ngketl6r0alg59w69ssckglfhfmgp64p).

##### Immunization Form Due Dates (2026-2027)

- Summer enrollment: form should be submitted by May 31, 2026

- Fall enrollment: form should be submitted after July 1, 2026

- Spring enrollment: form should be submitted by January 31, 2027

Visit the [Immunization Requirements](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-compliance/immunization-compliance) page and the [Immunization Requirements FAQ page](https://wellness.upenn.edu/faqs-immunization-requirements) for more information.

##### Need Immunizations?

Student Health and Counseling offers flu vaccines, vaccines needed for travel, and all of the vaccines needed to be compliant with University requirements.

[Schedule an appointment!](https://wellness.upenn.edu/appointments-0)

## Annual Insurance Requirements

All full-time and dissertation-status students, and exchange students here for a semester or more, must enroll in or waive the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP) annually, as all students must carry comprehensive health insurance as a condition of student enrollment at the University of Pennsylvania. If you have your own insurance coverage, you may waive enrollment in the Penn Student Insurance Plan. Please review the information below.

Please note: the PSIP portal will be open from April 15 through May 31 for students enrolled in the summer 2026 semester. For fall 2026 matriculants, the insurance portal will open July 1, 2026.

[Enroll or Waive: Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP)](https://studenthealth.bgenroll.com/home)

[Learn More About PSIP](https://wellness.upenn.edu/insurance-requirements/penn-student-insurance-plan-psip)

Watch this instructional video to find out how to complete your Insurance enrollment or waiver!

##### Clinical Fee

Wellness' Student Health and Counseling division is committed to partnering with you to treat illnesses and injuries, promote wellness, and provide you with health education and information. Access is provided through Penn's Clinical Fee. The clinical fee for the 2026-2027 academic year will be $385 per semester. All full-time students, including those who are enrolled in the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP), will be charged the Clinical Fee.

Visit the [Insurance Requirements](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-compliance/insurance-compliance) page for more information.

## Contact Our Immunization and Insurance Navigators

Please feel free to contact us with any questions. Please do not email us your immunization records, as they will not be processed.

The University of Pennsylvania requires all students to be compliant with the immunization requirements. Failure to meet these requirements will result in denial of student registration privileges. All students must submit their immunization information into their secure PennChart using the instructions below. You can also visit our [Immunization Requirements FAQ page](https://wellness.upenn.edu/faqs-immunization-requirements) for more information.

- [Universal Immunization Requirements: 2026-2027](https://upenn.box.com/s/vuf3dn6c0sn0vinekn4qp8tjequhwr8l)

Each School's form will be posted prior to the 2026-2027 academic year.

### Step 1: Contact your medical provider.

- Print the necessary immunization requirements form from the list above, complete the information, and have your medical provider review and sign it.

- Ask your medical provider for a copy of your full immunization records. Your provider should use the immunization form to provide a clearer picture of your immunization records prior to completing step 3.

- Scan or take a high-resolution photo of your complete and signed immunization form and other immunization records (please make certain the copy is legible and right side up).

### Step 2: Submit your immunization documents before your arrival to campus.

- Go to your [PennChart](https://secure.mypennmedicine.org/MyPennMedicine/Authentication/Login?) and log in. Please note: you will be directed to your PennChart through myPennMedicine. If you do not have an account, you will need to click on "Activate an Account."

- Once logged in, follow these [Immunization Requirements Submission Instructions](https://upenn.box.com/s/ngketl6r0alg59w69ssckglfhfmgp64p).

If you have questions, please contact the Immunization Navigators at [215-746-4200](tel:215-746-4200) or [wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu). For your medical privacy, do not email records to us.

##### Wellness at Penn: Statement about the University’s Immunization Requirements

Penn’s vaccination policy is informed by requirements from the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania as well as established scientific evidence demonstrating that immunizations are effective in preventing outbreaks and protecting the health and wellbeing of the campus population and its surrounding communities. These measures are especially important for safeguarding individuals who are under-vaccinated, unable to receive vaccines, or immunocompromised.

In alignment with the [Governor’s Executive Order 2025-02](https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/governor/documents/Executive%20Order%202025%2002%20Governor%20Shapiro%20Vaccines%20Access.pdf), Penn continues to rely on guidance from leading medical and public health authorities including, but not limited to, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), as well as the American College Health Association (ACHA). Our clinicians use this evidence-based guidance to support student health and promote a safe and healthy learning environment.

Penn remains committed to science-based public health practices and to fostering a campus environment in which all students can thrive.

##### Contact the Immunization Navigators

Please feel free to contact us with any questions. Please do not email us your immunization records, as they will not be processed. You can also visit our [Immunization Requirements FAQ page](https://wellness.upenn.edu/faqs-immunization-requirements) for more information.

#### Processes and Policies

### How do I submit my immunization records?

Visit the [Immunization Requirements](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-compliance/immunization-compliance) page for more information. You can also view our [Immunization Submission Instructions](https://upenn.box.com/s/04ehpwa7mmymrtpleebeutwx45hx6rln) to upload and submit your immunization information.

### I don’t have a PennChart account through myPennMedicine yet. What can I do?

If you don't have an existing myPennMedicine account, you must create and activate your account by clicking the button below. After you fill out this form, you will receive an email from our team with next steps within 2 business days. If you have questions, you can reach out to our Immunization Navigators by calling [215-746-4200](tel:215-746-4200) or emailing [wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu). You can also visit them in person at 3535 Market Street, Mezzanine, Suite 60.

[Activate Your PennChart](https://upenn-support.freshdesk.com/support/tickets/new?ticket_form=pennchart_account_activation_request_form)

### What should I do if I need to request a medical or religious exemption from an immunization?

The University's vaccine requirements exist to help protect the health and wellbeing of the entire campus community, including those who cannot be vaccinated or who choose not to be vaccinated. If you are seeking an exemption, please email [wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu) and identify whether it is a medical or religious exemption request. If you are living in on-campus housing, please also state whether the meningococcal vaccine is part of your request.

### What immunizations are required?

You can find the list of required immunizations here on the [Immunization Requirements](https://wellness.upenn.edu/immunization-insurance-compliance/immunization-compliance) page.

### I can’t find my immunization records; do I need to have my shots again?

If you aren't able to locate your immunization records, you must see a physician so that they can perform a test that will check your blood for antibodies. They can then enter this information on the Student Immunization Record. You can have these tests done at [Student Health and Counseling](https://wellness.upenn.edu/student-health-and-counseling) at your own expense, unless it is covered by your health insurance.

### How much do my immunizations cost?

Students with the Penn Student Insurance Plan (PSIP) are fully covered for required immunizations. In addition, the Affordable Care Act mandates that essential benefits, including certain immunizations and vaccines, be covered with no cost sharing. Please check with your health insurance carrier to see what vaccines are covered and how you can be reimbursed in the event that you obtain the immunizations at Student Health and Counseling. Learn more about vaccine costs here: [Wellness Vaccine and Titer Prices](https://upenn.box.com/s/dut3nitgx6nbr20fip3af5yreonv62np).

### I made a mistake on my online form, what should I do?

You should alert our Immunization and Insurance Navigators that the information you submitted is different than the information on your documentation. Your healthcare provider’s documentation is the document of record.

### What happens if I don't upload my immunization forms?

Failure to comply with the University’s immunization requirements and to submit the Student Immunization Record and/or the Student Medical History and Consent form will result in having a hold placed on your registration, which will make you unable to register and attend certain classes. If you do not have any online immunization information to enter, please alert the immunization office.

### I’m on registration hold. What do I do now?

First, check your messages in PennChart as there are likely instructions for next steps there. If there are not, contact our Immunization and Insurance Navigators. We can then explain why you are on hold and what you will need to do. Only the Immunization and Insurance Navigators can remove your hold. Because this involves your protected health information, we will NOT discuss this with third parties such as your school administration, professors, parents, or anyone else without your explicit consent.

### If I become compliant will I be taken off hold automatically?

No. The process is not automatic; it typically takes about 24 hours for a hold to be removed once you have become compliant. Please contact our Immunization and Insurance Navigators at 215-746-4200. Holds can only be removed during regular office hours.

### Do graduate students living off campus need to submit the immunization form AND documentation?

Non-healthcare graduate students living off campus can submit the immunization form OR documentation from a provider/previous University.

Healthcare graduate students must submit their immunization form AND documentation from a provider/previous University.

#### Requirements

### What is Penn’s TB testing requirement?

All full-time Penn students must complete an online TB risk factor screening questionnaire. Only those students who are considered to be in a high risk group for TB infection will need to be tested. Our Immunization and Insurance Navigators will contact you if you need to be tested for TB.

Healthcare students are required to submit a two-step PPD. The first step can be accepted from a US provider in last 12 months. The second step must be completed at Student Health and Counseling. IGRA blood test (Quantiferon TB Gold or T-Spot-TB) taken within last six months can take place of the two-step PPD.

### What are the options for TB testing?

Students whose TB screening questionnaire indicates that they need testing can either get a tuberculin skin test (also known as PPD) at Student Health and Counseling after they arrive on campus or they can get a TB blood test, such as the Quantiferon Gold or TSpotTB. Please note that Penn does not accept PPD tests that are administered outside of Student Health and Counseling. However, Penn does accept TB blood tests from outside healthcare providers that were performed within the past year (or within six months of entrance into Penn).

### What if I have had a positive test for TB infection in the past?

Students with a history of latent or active TB must schedule an appointment at Student Health and Counseling, and provide documentation of positive PPD skin test or IGRA blood test. Students must also submit a copy of their negative radiology report (chest x-ray performed in the US). International chest x-rays are not accepted. Films and CDs are not accepted. TB symptom checks are required annually.

### Do I have to be immunized against meningitis?

All incoming students who will be living in campus housing and who are age 21 or younger must submit proof of one dose on or after age 16 of meningococcal conjugate vaccine that covers serogroups A, C, Y, and W-135. Incoming students living on campus who are over age 21 should submit proof of vaccination on or after age 16 or request an exemption. If you are seeking an exemption, please email [wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu](mailto:wel-immun@pobox.upenn.edu) and identify whether it is a medical or religious exemption request for meningococcal vaccine.

### I live off campus. Do I have to have meningococcal immunization or submit a waiver?

No, you do not need to submit the waiver. Meningococcal vaccine is still recommended, but is not required, for students living off campus.

### I’m told that I can’t have the third hepatitis B vaccine for several months after the 2nd dose. What do I do?

We don’t require the third vaccine until your second semester. We will give you the proper time to finish the vaccine series.

### Does proof a Td vaccine satisfy the requirement for a Tdap vaccine?

No. The University of Pennsylvania requires a dose of Tdap (tetanus, diphtheria and acellular pertussis) within the past 10 years. Why? Guidance from the Philadelphia Department of Public Health and the American College Health Association recommend Tdap to help prevent outbreaks of pertussis on our campus. Pertussis immunity wains quickly, so the Tdap, instead of just a TD booster, offers the best protection in support of the health of our campus.

#### Requirements for Healthcare Students

### What if I have a negative Hepatitis B titer after 2 full series?

Healthcare students who have a negative Hepatitis B titer after two full series must submit two completed three-dose series AND submit two negative titers AND schedule a primary care appointment with Student Health and Counseling upon arrival to campus.

### What if I have a history of Hepatitis illness?

Healthcare students who have a history of Hepatitis illness must submit medical documentation and bloodwork reports AND schedule a primary care appointment with Student Health and Counseling upon arrival to campus.

### What if I have more questions?

You can call our Immunization and Insurance Navigators at 215-746-4200.

pages.md:
Student Health and Counseling offers solution-oriented, short-term care that is tailored to fit each student’s unique needs. Our services are free and confidential, and may be offered in-person and virtually in some circumstances. Nothing is too big or too small. Please remember, we are always available for urgent needs.

### Let's Talk and Drop-In Services

Let’s Talk

Let’s Talk provides access to free and confidential drop-in conversations with a trained professional at various locations across campus. Students can talk about any stress and anxiety they are feeling, bounce around ideas, and work through their emotions.

Some common concerns might include:

- Stress

- Sadness

- Difficulty adjusting to school

- Academic concerns

- Concentration and attention difficulty

- Family & financial problems

- Relationship concerns

[Learn More About Let's Talk](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/lets-talk)

Drop-In Services

Students can drop-in to the Student Health and Counseling office (3624 Market Street) at any time during regular business hours for counseling support.

### Psychiatric Medication Management

Our psychiatry team includes psychiatric nurse practitioners and psychiatrists who provide psychiatric evaluations, medication management, and case management to students in concurrent counseling who are seeking those services. Students can receive a referral for a psychiatric evaluation from their counselor. Since most psychological and emotional concerns are best addressed by counseling, psychiatry team members work in collaboration with their counseling colleagues to provide the most effective overall care for each student.

The following are important considerations before a student starts a psychotropic medication:

- If a student is wanting to start a medication near the end of the semester and is planning on leaving the Philadelphia area, it may not be possible for our psychiatry team members to start that medication. If the student leaves the area, the prescriber would not be able to provide the appropriate medical follow-up necessary to ensure the medication is working in a safe and effective manner. Initial prescriptions will likely not be written during and after the last two weeks of classes, however, students can be connected with our referral services to find care at their future location.

- If a student is already on medications prescribed by a member of our psychiatry team and is planning to be away for the summer or on a semester studying abroad, our team may continue to prescribe for the student depending on the stability of the student and the need for follow-up. Students will need to speak with their current prescriber about their care away from Philadelphia.

- Students must inform our psychiatry team members about their substance use before being prescribed medication. Substance use includes the regular use of alcohol, cannabis, vaping any substance, and the use of any illicit or controlled substance. Failure to disclose this information can result in serious consequences to the student’s health.

ADHD Care Navigation

If a student is seeking to establish or continue treatment for [Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)](https://www.cdc.gov/adhd/index.html), they should visit our [ADHD Care Navigation](https://wellness.upenn.edu/adhd) page. Academic accommodations are processed through the [Weingarten Center](https://wlrc.vpul.upenn.edu/), located at Hamilton Village (220 South 40th Street, Suite 260). They can be reached at [215-573-9235](tel:215-573-9235).

### Referral and Consultation Services

Why a Referral?

Our team provides short-term treatment that is tailored to students’ needs. Referrals to the community are ideal for students seeking longer-term or specialized treatment. Referrals are also used for students who are interested in psychoeducational testing, couples counseling and/or higher levels of care. Students may also seek referrals for a specific counseling approach or when seeking a provider of a specific identity or background. Students make the final decision about whether or not they can work with a particular outside provider.

- [Before the Referral](https://upenn.box.com/v/before-the-referral)

- [During the Referral](https://upenn.box.com/s/06vmdlkn1hkh1hdhttrcyb8t3d7s2obh)

- [After the Referral](https://upenn.box.com/v/after-the-referral)

Student Support

Contact our office for referral support. Students can also check out [Welltrack Connect](https://welltrack-connect.com/) page for support finding a therapist.

Online Students

View our [mental health resources for online students](https://upenn.box.com/s/jbqt865t7nlhpq1m6uaphv471gb0stjd).

### International Student Services

International students are a significant part of the Penn community. Student Health and Counseling recognizes that international students have unique needs, concerns, and strengths, while sharing common interests and goals with their American counterparts. Among the range of services that we provide for all Penn students, our counseling services staff offers tailored support and programming to international students.

- [International Student Programs and Resources](https://upenn.box.com/v/international-student-programs)

- [General Information (Mandarin)](https://upenn.box.com/s/ttmltoz8aw4lni8hy65zlrjnrorow77h)

- [Family Brochure (Mandarin)](https://upenn.box.com/s/ij315w52pl3na12s6af5fkxtzq8mw78q)

### Sexual Trauma Treatment Outreach and Prevention (STTOP)

The Sexual Trauma Treatment Outreach and Prevention (STTOP) Team is a multidisciplinary team of clinicians dedicated to providing confidential care, support, and advocacy to students who have experienced sexual trauma during their academic career. The culture of silence surrounding sexual assault and rape on campus and within our culture as a whole deters reporting, isolates victim-survivors, and undermines the safety and public health of all members of a community. The STTOP Team is committed to providing immediate support to students in need and to promoting awareness and change through active participation in campus outreach and collaboration with community partners.

Confidentiality

Student Health and Counseling offers confidential and free professional services to undergraduate, graduate and professional students at Penn. Students should call our team at [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) and select option 1 to speak with a mental health professional 24/7 or select option 2 to reach the front desk who can help schedule an appointment with a STTOP clinician. Students will be asked routine questions; it is their decision what details they feel comfortable disclosing. It is up to them whether they want to name or identify the offender. Students do not have to tell family members, academic programs, or law enforcement, and they do not have to file a report with the university in order to receive care.

Penn Violence Prevention

Penn Violence Prevention is a collaborative program which works to engage the Penn community in the prevention of sexual violence, relationship violence, and stalking on campus. For more information about resources on campus, reporting options, or how to support a friend, visit the [Penn Violence Prevention](https://pvp.universitylife.upenn.edu/) website.

Contact the STTOP Team Virtually

Students who have experienced rape, sexual assault, stalking or an unsafe or confusing sexual encounter should call our team at [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) to speak with a mental health professional 24/7.

Sexual Assault/Trauma Workshops

We offer a variety of workshops that center around conversations on intimacy, boundaries, safety, and trauma within relationships. Examples of topics include communicating consent, healthy/positive sexuality, and healthy relationships. We also provide safe spaces for individuals who identify as survivors to come together, find community, and cultivate pathways towards healing. Additionally, based on the principles of trauma-informed care, we offer workshops to support providers and caregivers on the impact of trauma on victim/survivor’s health and wellness.

Frequently Asked Questions

- Was what happened to me bad enough to count?  If you experienced an unsafe or confusing sexual encounter or relationship and you are considering reaching out to the STTOP team, we encourage you to do so. You do not need to put a label on your experience to receive help. You are entitled to respect and whatever support you need.

- Where can I find information on healthy sexuality?  It can be difficult to find information on healthy sexuality and sex positive behaviors. For more information on healthy sexuality including resources, glossaries, and scenarios for discussion, see the [National Sexual Violence Resource Center](https://www.nsvrc.org/find-help). Students are encouraged to sign up for [Vibe](https://wellness.upenn.edu/vibe), Wellness at Penn's digital sex education program.

- Where can I find other resources on campus?  For more information about resources, please visit our [Get Help Now](https://wellness.upenn.edu/get-help-now) page. You can also reach out to [Penn Violence Prevention](https://pvp.universitylife.upenn.edu/), [Special Services](https://www.publicsafety.upenn.edu/about/special-services/), the [Women’s Center](https://pwc.vpul.upenn.edu/), and [Student Health and Counseling](https://wellness.upenn.edu/student-health-and-counseling). We encourage students to reach out to whichever resource they feel most comfortable with.

- How can I support my friend?  Supporting a friend who has been assaulted, stalked or abused can be really hard. The role friends play in supporting survivors is essential, and it’s different from that of a counselor, lawyer, or doctor. For information about helping a friend, please visit the [Penn Violence Prevention](https://pvp.universitylife.upenn.edu/) website.

### LGBTQ+ Care

Wellness at Penn proudly supports our LGBTQ+ community with dedicated care that helps students feel seen, valued, and empowered. Whether they're exploring identity, navigating relationships, or forging their own path, our affirming therapists are here to listen, understand, and walk alongside them. Through the work of our LGBTQ+ Working Group, we collaborate with students, staff, and campus partners to ensure our services remain inclusive, responsive, and reflective of what our students need.

Our team offers one-on-one assessments and letters that meet professional standards and help support students considering or undergoing gender-affirming care. From exploring options to taking action, we’re here to support our students with clarity, compassion, and respect.

Learn more about our [LGBTQ+ Care](https://wellness.upenn.edu/medical-care/lgbtq-care).

## Contact Us

Counseling

[3624 Market Street, First Floor West, Philadelphia, PA 19104](https://www.google.com/maps?q=3624+Market+Street,%C2%A0First+Floor+West,%C2%A0Philadelphia,+PA+19104&sxsrf=ALiCzsZZ7C-rKC2eTqpSorw5TPm_AfsZfw:1667841691897&iflsig=AJiK0e8AAAAAY2lMq68RjduUQg3E6ChP3c9lQbgo9Wjb&uact=5&gs_lcp=Cgdnd3Mtd2l6EAMyCwguEIAEEMcBEK8BMgUIABCGAzIFCAAQhgNQAFgAYHRoAHAAeACAAVyIAVySAQExmAEAoAECoAEB&um=1&ie=UTF-8&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiUy8y9ypz7AhUiElkFHdrfBTQQ_AUoAXoECAIQAw)

24/7 Support

Call [215-746-WELL](tel:215-746-WELL) (9355) for information, support, to schedule an appointment, and to speak with an on-call provider.

pages.md:
###### Wellness at Penn is committed to fostering a campus culture where every student feels seen, supported, and empowered. We provide compassionate care, inclusive mental health resources, and 24/7 access to critical support.

This page is part of our ongoing suicide prevention and mental health support efforts.

### Crisis & Hotline Contact Information

In an Emergency:

- On Campus (PennComm): 215-573-3333

- Off Campus: Call 911

Suicide Prevention & Mental Health Hotlines:

- National Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Dial 988

- Crisis Text Line: Text HOME to 741741

- Trevor Project (LGBTQ+ youth): 1-866-488-7386 or text START to 678678

- Trans Lifeline: 1-877-565-8860

- Veterans Crisis Line: 1-800-273-8255 or text 838255

- National Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-799-SAFE (7233) or text START to 88788

- RAINN (Sexual Assault): 1-800-656-HOPE (4673)

- Penn Student Health and Counseling (24/7): 215-746-WELL (9355)

[View Get Help Now Resources](https://wellness.upenn.edu/get-help-now)

### Crisis Intervention Resources

Students can speak with a trained mental health professional any time, any day:

- Call 24/7: 215-746-WELL (9355)

- Drop-In: 3624 Market Street, First Floor West (during normal business hours)

- Let's Talk: drop-in conversations with trained mental health professionals at various locations across campus. [Learn more here](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/lets-talk).

Other 24/7 Penn Support:

- Public Safety & MERT: 215-573-3333

- Special Services (Support for crime, sexual violence): 215-898-6600

- Walking Escort Program: 215-898-WALK

- Penn HELP Line: 215-898-HELP (4357)

### Mental Health Resources & Access

We encourage all students to prioritize mental wellness and know support is always within reach.

Clinical Offerings Include:

- [Individual Therapy](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/individual-therapy) & [Group Therapy](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/group-therapy)

- [Peer Support](https://wellness.upenn.edu/peer-support) & “[Let’s Talk](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/lets-talk)”

- [Teletherapy via Mantra Health](https://wellness.upenn.edu/teletherapy) (virtual 1:1 support)

- Referrals for Specialized or Long-Term Care

Online students have access to emergency care and referrals at no cost.

Call 215-746-WELL(9355) for more information and [Learn More About Our Counseling Resources here.](https://wellness.upenn.edu/student-health-and-counseling)

### Multimedia & Educational Resources

Wellness at Penn uses a variety of tools to help our community recognize warning signs, take action, and access support.

Featured Resources:

- [be aware](https://wellness.upenn.edu/be-aware): Asynchronous online training on mental health and support skills

- [i share Video](https://vimeo.com/734751960): Penn students share their experiences with mental health

- [i care Training](https://wellness.upenn.edu/i-care-i-share-be-aware/i-care): In-person training to support students in distress

- [Stress, Distress & Crisis Guide](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/caring-yourself-and-others-stress-distress-and-crisis): Self-help and peer-support tools

These resources are accessible to all students, faculty, and staff year-round.

### Student Communication & Outreach

Penn’s mental health resources are communicated to students in multiple ways throughout the year, including:

- Our Website

  - [Public Health & Wellbeing](https://wellness.upenn.edu/public-health-and-wellbeing)

  - [Wellbeing Initiatives](https://wellness.upenn.edu/public-health-wellbeing/wellbeing-initiatives)

- Campus-wide Emails through our [Student Newsletter](https://us12.campaign-archive.com/home/?u=b1e6259a71b022c9c892651b2&id=438c13282c)

  - Sent to all incoming students at the start of the year

  - Sent to all students at the beginning of each semester

- Social Media

  - Follow us for regular wellness tips and updates: [Instagram @wellnessatpenn](https://www.instagram.com/wellnessatpenn)

- Tabling, Peer Education, & Events

  - Including annual Send Silence Packing, National Public Health Week, and more.

- Collaborations with LGBT Center, Penn Violence Prevention, and other campus offices

- Podcast:

  - [Campus Conversations – Listen on Spotify](https://wellness.upenn.edu/campus-conversations)

### Post- Intervention & Community Support

In the unfortunate event of a student suicide or crisis, Penn follows a structured communication and care protocol:

- Campus-wide communication is sent via email from the University leadership

- Close contacts (friends, classmates, RAs, etc.) receive follow-up from Wellness at Penn staff

- All communications include links to available support services and resources

- Additional healing spaces, debriefs, and support groups may be provided

## "i share"

This video was created by Wellness at Penn and student leaders to promote sharing with others and getting support in times of stress, distress, and crisis. Learn more about [Caring for Yourself and Others: Stress, Distress, and Crisis](https://wellness.upenn.edu/counseling/caring-yourself-and-others-stress-distress-and-crisis).

## Need Immediate Help and Support?

Call 215-746-WELL (9355)

Dial 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

[Get Help Now](https://wellness.upenn.edu/get-help-now)

You are never alone. Support is available, whenever you need it.

###### Insurance Navigation

All full time, dissertation and exchange students (in classes for one term or longer) are required to have comprehensive health insurance. The [Penn Student insurance Plan (PSIP)](https://wellness.upenn.edu/insurance-requirements/penn-student-insurance-plan-psip) is available for students who do not have insurance, whose plans do not provide coverage in the Philadelphia area, or whose plans do not meet our criteria for alternative insurance.
